steps.content: In just one night, a stack of complaint letters as thick as half a coin piles up on the desk.

There are all sorts of Sinners in the Bureau. Those who like to play the guitar, those who like to dance, those who like to raise flowers or animals... And usually, you respect their innocuous little hobbies.

But this newcomer Dudu really puts you in a bind. She loves to play the same song on her suona over and over again. At first, everyone was entertained by something new, but after a while, no one can stand it anymore.

You've talked to her several times about this, but she's sly and can't be persuaded. She'll simply agree to your demands and then keep doing what she always does. Recently, there are even signs of her behavior worsening...
Her blaring suona kept you up all night last night. Judging from these complaints, you weren't the only one.
A burst of footsteps snaps you out of your thoughts. Nightingale has come to tell you that both the venue and Dudu are ready for you.
You shake your head and stand up, taking along the stack of complaints.
Let's go.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Hey boss, you're finally here? Sleep well last night?
Dudu starts blabbering eagerly as soon as you sit down across from her.
This little girl is always full of life and sociable, yet there always seems to be some wicked intentions lurking beneath her toothy grin.
She leans forward, observing you carefully.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Oh no, the dark circles under your eyes tell me you didn't. In that case... I'll play you a song on my suona to cheer you up? Since you're the boss, I'll give you a 20% discount for listening...

As she speaks, she takes out the incriminating "weapon" as if revealing a treasure, the precious suona that she forbids anyone to touch. Once, when someone touched it out of curiosity, Dudu almost pounced on him in a fit of rage.
No, thanks.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Huh? Did I charge you too much? Don't worry, the price is negotiable. A 50% discount, then...
That's enough. Check these out.
You cut her off, and push the stack of complaint letters towards her.
She looks around, then suddenly lowers her voice mysteriously.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Cough cough. I'll give you a 50% discount, but don't tell the others. It'll be a secret between us.
She looks at you eagerly, but doesn't get a reply.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Uhh... Why aren't you saying anything?
Are you done? Then let's get to the topic.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: The topic? You're not here to listen to my music?
You don't reply, but just push the complaint letters towards her.
Look at these.
test
test
test
test
test
test
Dudu's gaze follows your hands and lands on the pile of letters. Her eyes widen incredulously.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: These are...?
You pick out a few at random, clear your throat and start reading them out loud.
"Chief, I haven't been able to shut my eyes for three whole days because of that damn suona. The dark circles under my eyes are so thick that the alarm goes off when the sensors scan my face."
"Chief, I feel like I'm in the countryside again, only the roosters back home don't crow as much as she does."
"I'm going insane. If I hear that song one more time, I'll put poison on her mouthpiece at night. I'll really do it! It's me or the suona... One of us has to go!"
After reading out these complaints, you can't help but worry about everyone's mental health. Dudu's smile fades.
I remember warning you multiple times not to play that song all day and night. If this continues, I'll have no choice but to confiscate your suona.
Sure enough, the words "confiscate your suona" instantly makes her panic and yell at you.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Who gives you the right to confiscate my suona?!

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: How is me playing the suona any different from the combat training y'all do? You know what'll happen if I don't practice and get rusty? My livelihood depends on it!

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Plus, my teacher taught me this piece back in the day. It's the one I play best!

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: I was like this back in the Drifter Camp. I'd go play whenever there was a wedding or funeral, and if there were none, I'd just play by the roadside.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Everyone in the Drifter Camp loves hearing me play. The generous ones even give me money. I really don't get why you folks at the Bureau hate it so much.
Her lips tremble, as if she had just suffered a grave injustice.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Since y'all find me so annoying, just let me go home! This place cramps my style anyways...
You mean to the Drifter Camp?

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Of course. Where else?
If I remember correctly, aren't you an Outlander? You couldn't have been in the Drifter Camp for more than a few years.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: So? The Drifter Camp is the place that truly accepts me. It's my home.
Dudu snorts, unimpressed.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: So what if I haven't been there that long? I know the Drifter Camp as well as any local!

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Let me put it this way. Even if you drop me into the Drifter Camp blindfolded, I can tell which street I'm on by the smell alone.
Are you being serious?
Though her tone is calm and convincing, you can't help but wonder if she's mixed the real with the imaginary.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Of course I'm being serious!

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Who's the biggest spender, who you should never cross, which part of the river is best for catching fish, which forest grove is best for a date, who sells the yummiest stinky tofu, whose cat catches the most mice, who's the best matchmaker in the camp... I know the answers to all these questions!
She pauses, her eyes shifting about. Heaven knows what tricks are popping into her head.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Hmm... If you don't believe me, I'll give you a consultation for free.
For free? Knowing you, shouldn't you be extorting some sort of fee?
You raise your brows in surprise.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Pfft, I make my money from honest work, okay? How can you call it "extortion"... Anyways, back to the subject. I'm doing you a big favor this time. Ask me anything you want. If I can't answer it, I'll swap the syllables of my name back to front!
...But wouldn't that still be Dudu?
Your mouth twitches. You calm yourself down, trying your best not to let her ruin your composure.
This little girl had tricked you many times before, so you're always extra vigilant when dealing with her. Even now, you're keenly aware that she's goading you to ask her about the Drifter Camp.
In that case... It's better to just go along and see what tricks she has up her sleeve.
Then... Did anything major happen in the Drifter Camp recently?

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Anything major...
Dudu rubs her chin, thinks for a moment, then flashes a confident smile.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Of course there has!

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: A goose escaped from the market and chased the blacksmith's youngest son for three miles straight. This trauma has left him with a deep fear of birds, and now he pees his pants at the honk of a goose.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: The egg seller's daughter plucked a bunch of chicken feathers to make a shuttlecock, but she spooked her family's hens so much that they stopped laying eggs. Her mother beat her up for this.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Our building manager's son is getting married next month. He's ecstatic and preparing a huge wedding. I must go and play him a song or two.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Ah, there's more! The old lady who lives next door to me hasn't been in the best health. She felt that she didn't have much time left, so she asked me to help arrange her funeral...
Even though it was just a casual question, you can't help but cut off her incessant blabbering. These petty trivialities couldn't be farther from "anything major."
I asked if "anything major" happened. Maybe you can pick some important things to talk about.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: These things aren't important? They may seem meaningless to you, but for us in the Drifter Camp, these things make up our daily lives.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: We're not like you. We don't have any lofty ideals. Survival is our only pursuit. So yeah, those things are pretty major to us.
Her stubborn, willful gaze puts you out of words.
...Sorry, you're right. I didn't think of it that way. I shouldn't have said that.
A look of astonishment flashes across her face. She obviously didn't expect you to apologize. After regaining her focus, she rubs her nose and coughs awkwardly.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Cough... Okay, okay. I forgive you.
That little episode makes you curious about the source of her news, so you take the lead in breaking the ice.
Where did you get all that news from?

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Ah, well that requires some technique.
Perhaps you're just imagining it, but you feel that Dudu has become more relaxed and sincere towards you.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: The best places in the Drifter Camp to get news are: the riverside where ladies wash clothes in the evening, the night market stalls where people grab food after work, the game tables of senior citizens, and the roadside where the Homeless beg.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Each of these places has it pros and cons.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: The laundry ladies aren't very vigilant. They start chatting nonstop whenever they bump into someone, but it's usually just neighborhood gossip that won't interest you.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: You can get a wider variety of news from where the workers gather. These aren't limited to just neighborhood gossip. After all, they have diverse sources. But these middle-aged men love to brag, so a lot of it is hearsay.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: As for the elderly, they've lived a long time and have seen a lot, but often their minds are a bit muddled, so it's easy for them to forget the details of past events.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: The Homeless are everywhere in the Drifter Camp. Nothing escapes their eyes and ears. Getting news from them is often the most efficient choice, and their news is the most accurate. But these guys are very greedy, and will probably try to rip you off.
You listen quietly and intently to Dudu. It seems that she really knows the Drifter Camp like the back of her hand, and has a lot of experience gathering information.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: So how about it, boss? Now do you believe how well I know the camp?
I believe you.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: In that case, I have another brilliant idea. Want to hear it?
Sure enough, she can't wait to let the cat out of the bag. This is exactly what you've been waiting for.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Why don't you send me to the Drifter Camp for a while to gather news for you?

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: I know that the MBCC is now in contact with the Drifter Camp. You probably need a lot of intelligence. As someone who is intimately familiar with the place and won't raise suspicion from the locals, I'm your best choice.
You listen to her premeditated proposal and smirk.
So after leading me down the garden path, this is what you really wanted to say?
Though a bit annoyed that you didn't take the bait, she continues to push for her cause.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Well, that way, not only will I get to keep my suona and livelihood, you also don't have to worry about looking after me, and no one's life will be disturbed. Isn't it a win-win?
…Sorry, the MBCC has no precedent for releasing detained Sinners. We also have dedicated agents for gathering intelligence.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: What... So it's still a no after all that. I wasted my breath for nothing.
She mumbles quietly to herself, her fawning grin vanishing from her face. But your heart softens upon seeing her so upset.
Though I can't let you go back, I can ask the intelligence agents to regularly share information with you about the camp.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: For real? Are you being serious? You're not pulling my leg?
Dudu looks at you in surprise, lifting her head as if she has heard something unbelievable.
Of course I'm being serious. I'm not that cold-hearted.
Having gotten an affirmative answer, Dudu beams with joy, her eyes squinting from her fawning smile.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Having some information to hear is better than nothing! No wonder you're the Chief of the MBCC! You're so wise and caring towards the masses!

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: What are they?
From today onwards, you must abide by the Bureau's work and rest schedule. You may only play the suona at specified times and places, and you must not disturb other people's rest.
If you violate any of these conditions, the information sharing will cease immediately.
She salutes you goofily with a playful smile.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Roger that! Don't worry boss, I promise I'll be good!
You tell Nightingale to take Dudu back. Watching her skip happily behind Nightingale, you finally let out a sigh of relief.
A wave of exhaustion sweeps over you. After reaching a deal with this little troublemaker, you can finally live a few days in peace.
